demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

Memory.value: I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind.
When I remember the event I feel intense rage
Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning

Negative Appraisals.value: Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore
I acted in ways that go against who I am
The event happened because of the way I acted

issues.item: Memory Feels Alien: The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me
issues.explanation: The trauma type is accidentally causing serious injury to another person. 'Memory Feels Alien' can occur in PTSD, but paired with the available appraisal pattern it suggests stronger dissociation/self-detachment than is otherwise represented; more importantly, the memory cluster centers on fragmented visual recall and rage, whereas the appraisal cluster centers on guilt/meaning plus personal bodily damage, making the profile feel pulled between different trauma experiences.

issues.item: Physical Vulnerability: My body has been permanently damaged by what happened
issues.explanation: 'Physical Vulnerability: My body has been permanently damaged by what happened' is hard to reconcile with the indexed trauma type, which is causing serious injury to another person rather than being physically injured oneself. Unless the event also seriously injured the patient, this item is clinically implausible. It also does not fit well with the Memory → Negative Appraisals formulation, because the memory items provided more naturally support guilt, shame, or moral injury appraisals such as 'Violated Values' rather than permanent bodily damage.

vignette: Rahul's hands moved with a practiced ease as he methodically cleaned the upscale condominium, his mind a thousand miles away. It had been months since the incident at work, but the memories still lingered, snapshots in his mind that refused to fade. He recalled the sound of shattering glass, the look of shock on his coworker's face, and the feeling of weightlessness as he watched her fall down the stairs. The images played out like a gruesome slideshow, each moment frozen in time. As he polished the banister, Rahul's thoughts drifted back to that fateful day. He had been hurrying to finish his tasks, eager to meet his deadline, when disaster struck. In his haste, he had knocked over a bucket of cleaning solution, causing it to spill down the stairs. His coworker, rushing to help, lost her footing and tumbled down the stairs, suffering serious injuries. The memory still haunted Rahul, filling him with intense rage whenever it surfaced. He couldn't understand why he had been so careless, why he hadn't taken the extra few seconds to ensure his safety and that of others. As Rahul worked, the familiar sounds and smells of the condominium - the hum of the vacuum, the scent of fresh cleaning products - triggered memories of the incident without warning. It was as if his mind had created an Pavlovian response, linking these innocuous stimuli to the traumatic event. The sudden recall left him reeling, his thoughts spiraling down a rabbit hole of self-blame and recrimination. He tormented himself with questions: Why had he been so reckless? Had he deliberately put others at risk? The memories also stirred up feelings of meaninglessness and disconnection. Rahul felt as though the event had shaken the foundations of his life, leaving him questioning everything he thought he knew about himself. Nothing seemed to hold significance anymore - not his work, not his relationships, not even his own identity. He struggled to reconcile the person he was before the incident with the one he had become after. The values he once held dear - responsibility, compassion, and kindness - now seemed like distant ideals, irreparably tarnished by his actions. As Rahul finished cleaning the condominium, he couldn't shake off the feeling of emptiness that had been growing inside him for months. He felt lost, adrift in a world that no longer made sense to him. The memories continued to plague him, fueling his self-doubt and eroding his confidence. It was this overwhelming sense of disintegration that finally drove Rahul to seek help, hoping to find a way to piece together the fragments of his shattered life. Rahul's eyes wandered around the spotless condominium, now quiet and still, a stark contrast to the turmoil brewing within him. He knew he couldn't continue living like this, forever trapped in a cycle of guilt, anger, and self-loathing. As he packed up his cleaning supplies and headed out into the unknown, Rahul felt a glimmer of hope - perhaps, with the right guidance, he could learn to reassemble the pieces of his life, rediscover meaning, and find forgiveness for himself.
